disposition_mapping.rationale: The calendar and assumptions issuance function persists but is expanded into a version-controlled scenario library covering the required downside scenario, serving as the single assumption source for all downstream steps.

Top-down target setting is unconstrained by design but is retained and improved by conditioning targets on the new scenario library rather than a single central case, giving the CEO/CFO visibility into downside sensitivity when setting targets.
Revenue and volume planning ownership and inputs/outputs are unchanged; only the authoring tooling (driver-based templates) is modernised, satisfying the requirement that this function survive.

Cost centre and headcount budgeting ownership and inputs/outputs are unchanged; driver-based automation reduces build effort without altering the owner-accountability model, satisfying the step-preservation requirement.
Capex request submission is preserved and still mandatorily consumes a business case for requests above threshold, now enforced by workflow routing rather than manual check, satisfying ABB-R-04.

Consolidation into the draft three-statement budget is preserved as a function and continues to consume accounting policies applied to actuals and central FX assumptions (ABB-R-05, ABB-R-07); automation of consolidation and reconciliation restructures how the work is done without removing it, satisfying ABB-R-06.

Review-and-challenge is unconstrained by design and is merged with a new mandatory downside stress-test, strengthening the challenge process the board will rely on, while the underlying iterative negotiation with submitters continues.

Board approval remains a distinct governance gate consuming the revised budget, now also informed by stress-test results, satisfying ABB-R-11 and preserving the ordering precondition required by ABB-R-08.

Loading and locking of the approved version is preserved and occurs strictly after board approval (ABB-R-08, ABB-R-09); automated system loading and enforced locking replace manual steps but the control function is unchanged.

steps.description: FP&A issues the budget calendar and central planning assumptions (inflation, FX, interest rates) together with a library of macro scenarios, including at least one downside scenario, built in the integrated planning platform so all submitters plan against a common, version-controlled assumption set.
steps.name: Issue calendar, central planning assumptions and scenario library

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets using a driver-based model that runs the strategic plan against the central and downside scenarios, producing targets that are explicitly scenario-conditioned rather than single-point.
steps.name: Set top-down targets via driver-based scenario modelling

steps.description: Business unit heads prepare and own revenue and volume plans in driver-based templates within the integrated planning platform, with FP&A analysts providing system support; ownership and approval accountability are unchanged from the baseline.
steps.name: Revenue and volume plans

steps.description: Cost centre owners prepare and own cost centre and headcount budgets using driver-based templates (headcount, rate, activity drivers) that auto-populate from HR and central assumptions, reducing manual spreadsheet build while preserving owner accountability.
steps.name: Cost centre and headcount budgets

steps.description: Business unit heads submit capex requests through an embedded workflow that mandatorily attaches and routes a business case for any request above the materiality threshold before it can enter the consolidation, strengthening evidential support over the baseline's manual attachment.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests with embedded business-case workflow

steps.description: The planning system consolidates revenue, cost, headcount and capex submissions into a draft three-statement budget prepared on the same accounting basis and policies as actuals, applying the central FX assumptions to translate multi-currency submissions and automatically reconciling the P&L, balance sheet and cash flow, reducing manual reconciliation effort versus the baseline.
steps.name: Automated consolidation into draft three-statement budget

steps.description: FP&A and CFO review and challenge the draft budget in iterations with submitters, now including a mandatory stress-test of the revised budget against the downside scenario from the scenario library before the version is finalised for board submission.
steps.name: Iterative review, challenge and scenario stress-test

steps.description: The board reviews the revised budget together with its downside stress-test results and approves the budget, unchanged in substance from the baseline governance gate.
steps.name: Board approval

steps.description: The approved budget is automatically loaded into the EPM system and locked as the single version used by variance analysis, with system-enforced edit locks replacing manual version control; occurs only after, and is gated by, board approval.
steps.name: Load and lock approved budget version
